title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: GUS GOES INLAND
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Gus Medeiros, a scallop fisherman from New Bedford, Massachusetts.
Forty-five years on the ocean. Then, at seventy-one, his knees said, that's enough, Captain.
His daughter Lucia said, come live with us in Omaha, Nebraska.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: LEAVING THE DOCK
segments.quote: The fishermen know that the sea is dangerous and the storm terrible, but they have never found these dangers sufficient reason for remaining ashore.
segments.author: Vincent van Gogh
lines: Gus said no three times. New places scared him more than storms.
By the boat's wheel hung an old postcard from the painter Vincent van Gogh:
The fishermen know that the sea is dangerous and the storm terrible, but they have never found these dangers sufficient reason for remaining ashore.
So Gus sold the boat and drove west.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: THE SOUP
segments.quote: The ache for home lives in all of us, the safe place where we can go as we are and not be questioned.
segments.author: Maya Angelou
lines: He ate canned chowder alone in the spare room. It tasted like a sad envelope.
Lucia left him a Maya Angelou book, one line marked:
The ache for home lives in all of us, the safe place where we can go as we are and not be questioned.
So Gus cooked his mother's Portuguese kale soup. The house smelled like home.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: THE FARMER
segments.quote: There are only two or three human stories, and they go on repeating themselves as fiercely as if they had never happened before.
segments.author: Willa Cather
lines: Across the street lived Arlen, a retired corn farmer who waved like it cost him money.
At the library, Gus found Willa Cather, Nebraska's great novelist:
There are only two or three human stories, and they go on repeating themselves as fiercely as if they had never happened before.
Weather, debt, four a.m. alarms. Same story, different water. Gus brought Arlen soup, and they talked till dark.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: THIN ICE
segments.quote: I know not all that may be coming, but be it what it will, I'll go to it laughing.
segments.author: Herman Melville
lines: In January, Arlen took him ice fishing. Gus had never stood on top of the fish before.
His boots shot out. Flat on his back.
He remembered Herman Melville, who wrote about New Bedford whalers:
I know not all that may be coming, but be it what it will, I'll go to it laughing.
So he laughed until Arlen laughed too. Then he caught a catfish uglier than his old boat.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: THE FISH FRY
segments.quote: A man can be destroyed but not defeated.
segments.author: Ernest Hemingway
lines: Gus planned a fish fry for the block. The oil got too hot. Every fillet came out black.
Thirty neighbors were coming. He sat in the garage, ready to cancel.
On his shelf sat The Old Man and the Sea, by Ernest Hemingway:
A man can be destroyed but not defeated.
At dawn, he and Arlen went back and caught twenty more.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: THE BLOCK
segments.author: Rachel Carson
lines: Saturday, Gus fried alone, panicking.
Then Arlen brought sweet corn, the Nguyens brought rice, and somebody brought lemonade.
Lucia quoted the scientist Rachel Carson:
In nature nothing exists alone.
Now the whole street calls him Captain, and nobody eats canned chowder.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Leave the dock. Make a home. Find your story. Laugh. Try again. Never alone.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Leave the dock. Make a home. Find your story in someone new. Laugh when you fall. Try again. Never alone.
I went ice fishing once. The fish won, and so did the ice.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
